verdict.rationale: Homebrew's documented tap system lets developers add third-party repositories of formulae, casks and external commands via `brew tap <user>/<repo>`, remove them with `brew untap`, and trust individual items. Community reports confirm people use and host taps, and welcome the new tap-trust feature, though one user found hosting a tap harder than an apt/yum repo because it needs a git server. brew bundle also extends to other package backends such as Go, Cargo, uv, npm and Flatpak. Missing for 10: detailed documentation on authoring external-command plugins, and a static-host (non-git) tap distribution option.
